study.question: Can a small learned target-conditioned router retain useful within-block event content before compression, beyond a matched history-conditioned router, and does its quality/cost depend on compression density?
study.hypothesis: Observation: the source-gated UF incumbent remains best on click at 0.660646940486458. Target exact-match grouping in round0 did not beat rotated/uniform grouping (0.657258 versus 0.657516/0.657469), so exact-match stratification is not supported. Action-stratification and residual branches were also unsuccessful on click. Exact-count round6, aligned moments round7 and nonlinear codes round8 stayed below the incumbent. In round8, before-pool versus after-pool encoding yielded 0.659937903 versus 0.659958564 with blocked sources, and 0.658548415 versus 0.658525238 with shared sources; nonlinear timing has no meaningful measured advantage in those implementations. Auxiliary quality partially recovered with those sidecars, so their failure is specific to click selection and not total absence of value. Mechanism hypothesis: a fixed block mean can wash out target-relevant events before downstream scoring. Cheap bounded low-rank attention can condition which content is retained inside the fixed UF partition without new ID tables or an expensive full-history DIN scorer. A history-centroid query is the active capacity-matched retrieval control. Half uniform mass and exact downstream counts preserve broad coverage and an exposure scale, but do not imply a sufficient statistic or exact intensity preservation.

nearest_work.difference: Read archived exact-version primary text lines235-274: target-specific event activation and unnormalized interest-intensity aggregation. Inherit DIN-style query/key/product interactions and unnormalized downstream activation; add only local softmax inside compressed blocks with a uniform mixture and count multiplier. This is an adaptation of established attention, with no priority claim.

Inspected pinned implementation lines30-170 and190-274: feature-conditioned and fixed queries, recent/earlier sequence partitions, dot-product retrieval followed by heterogeneous mixing. Adapt the conditional-query idea into one rank-16 bounded cosine router within fixed temporal/feedback blocks. No learned query-token bank, full tokenizer, recent/earlier split or heterogenous mixer is reproduced. Original paper detail unavailable through authorized reader; equivalence and novelty remain unverified.

Inspected pinned lines81-160: queries generated from context/target/sequence mean, with iterative sequence/global-token interaction. Here target versus historical mean is a controlled replacement at the first compression operator; no iterative sequence stack or global-token decoder is adopted.
Original link verified; authorized read reports detailed text unavailable and a labeled benchmark fallback. No full-paper mechanism, reproduction or novelty claim is made.

The entry candidate.py implements the source-gated UF incumbent operator; exact numerical initialization equality is a host prerequisite. Retain its features, shared action-aware DIN scorer, task towers and gradient permissions; replace uniform within-block compression with mixed uniform/attention means. No round6-8 sidecars are inherited.

inherited_components: Frozen released fields, feature embeddings, pre-padded 100-event history and task masks
Incumbent 10-block UF semantics: uniform click route and two auxiliary feedback strata per block; 20-block alternative is predeclared
Action-aware shared DIN local activation, four task MLP towers, sum of four unweighted BCEs
Detached auxiliary scorer parameters and item/action paths; open supplied context gradients; primary-owned Dice buffers
New module allocation after inherited reset with restoring CPU RNG scope
study.proposed_difference: Replace each arithmetic block/stratum mean by 0.5*uniform_mean+0.5*attention_mean. Bias-free key and query projections have rank16. Score each visible event using twice the cosine similarity between its item/action key and either the target item-fields query or the masked historical item-fields mean query. Each slot normalizes only over its own valid members and is zero if empty. Compute both query projections in every cell. Retain exact per-slot counts in downstream unnormalized DIN pooling. Cross query source with 10 versus20 blocks (30 versus60 total scorer slots); four models have identical parameter shapes. Auxiliary losses see detached summaries, so they cannot change router parameters. No new data, labels, loss hook, exact joins, count sidecars or code heads.
predictions: At a fixed block count, target-conditioned compression should improve validation click AUC over the active history-query replacement if current-target relevance is useful before averaging. It should also beat the incumbent to justify selection.
A larger target-over-history gap with10 than20 blocks would be compatible with target retrieval offsetting stronger compression, subject to Dice and optimization confounds. No sign is guaranteed.

The router should produce finite nonuniform coefficients on heterogeneous nonempty blocks; changing the authorized target while fixing history should change target-mode summaries. In history mode, the compression alone must be invariant to target changes; final predictions need not be.

Empty strata have exactly zero means/counts, nonempty row coefficients sum to1, and padding perturbations never change compressed outputs or predictions. Auxiliary-loss gradients into router/scorer and item/action computational paths are zero; context/tower paths remain trainable.

Added projection work covers100 events at rank16; expensive downstream scorer covers30/60 slots rather than100. Total speedup is uncertain and must be measured, including BF16/FP32 casts and inference.
falsifiers: Finite but nonuniform target routing that fails to beat the history-query replacement and incumbent on paired validation comparisons gives no support for this proposed useful-content mechanism.

Uniform or target-insensitive routing means this implementation did not exercise the hypothesized conditional selection; it is an implementation/optimization null, not general refutation of target-conditioned compression.
A similar improvement for target and history queries supports learned content pooling or capacity rather than current-target conditioning.
A gain only when using20 blocks does not establish cheap compression benefits; if its measured cost dominates the incumbent without reliable quality improvement, reject the efficiency claim.

Any masking leak, current-label dependence, wrong target action usage, gradient ownership mismatch, nonfinite values, unexpected parameter mismatch or budget overrun blocks admissibility before interpreting predictive metrics.
alternative_explanations: The single-pass low dense learning rate may not train a new router enough; cosine saturation or low input norm could hide the intended intervention.
Apparent gains may follow changed gradient routing, extra dense parameters, regularization or Dice distributions rather than retained target-relevant content.
The 1/2 uniform mixture and bounded scores could be too conservative; one unsuccessful implementation would not disprove the mechanism.
Single-seed sampling and repeated user exposures limit uncertainty estimates; repeated architectural trends are not independent seed replications.
Auxiliary-source blocking repeatedly favored click but substantially damaged auxiliary AUC. This suite retains that tradeoff, and does not claim balanced four-task success.
